data.name: Call of the Ocean
data.detailed_description:
Call of the Ocean is a VR exploration game set in and around the ocean, with a variety of ocean creatures and locations to discover.

Set mainly in an island lagoon filled with ancient Greek temples and artefacts, the game integrates motion controls for full freedom of movement including swimming, climbing, running and jumping.

This game is in Early Access, but the motion controls, locations and creatures are in a playable state. You can explore ancient temples and shipwrecks, admire the beautiful wildlife, swim and play with dolphins. Grab hold and tag along for a ride on a turtle or whale. Cage dive with sharks - or better yet, dare your family and friends to go out of the cage and swim with them!

Further game maps and features are in development, to be included into the existing game.

reviews.review:
This is exactly the type of VR experience I have wanted. It is what I wish theBlu was. You can just swim around peacefully among humpback whales, or sharks, or explore a lagoon paradise with surprises all over the place. You never know what animals you will run into. I can easily spend hours in here. So relaxing.

Praise aside, there are definitely things that need to be improved though. The swimming animations are pretty good when fish/mammals are moving straight ahead, but as soon as they change direction, you remember they are fake. They turn awkwardly on an axis and its very unnatural. But certainly it is something I'm sure they will improve upon.

Some other things that I noticed:
- The handheld jetpack thing sits in your hand at such an awkward angle. It would be better if your hand was in the middle of it rather than on an end.
- The climbing is a little buggy. It's hard to know when you are grabbing something or if you're going to fall. I got a little frustrated trying to climb across the rocks and ropes. It should just be easier to keep with the relaxing vibe of everything else.
- The scale of the small fish is very off. Not sure if the developers care about this level of realism or not. But the clownfish and damselfish are the same size as the tangs and angels, however they should be much smaller. Also, some fish species were perfectly designed (several clownfish species were so well done, they were just too big), and some fish were like weird combinations of species. Again, not sure if the developers are going for exact realism here. I have a saltwater tank so I happen to know reef fish more than the average person.

It's early access so I expect many impropvements, but what is already here is really really great. Well worth the 8 dollars. I can't wait to see what is added in the future. 

Excuse me, I'm going to go back to exploring the lagoon.
reviews.developer_response:
Thanks for the encouraging review Brett, a year ago I also wished there were more games with freedom of movement out there, so I decided to try making one myself!

You have made several good points for improvement - I'll look at making the climbing easier. In the meantime the trick I use for climbing is to hold the grab button before reaching for a ledge, and you will feel the controller vibrate and snap on to the ledge once you have found a suitable position.

You are right that I have plans to improve the creature movement, I am planning to rework the whale movement from physical drag equations so that it has more natural and beautiful movement rather than typical video game character movement. I will also look at varying the fish sizes and behaviour more now that we've got all the basics elements in place.

I hope you continue to enjoy the game!
